title: Hempstead Plains Preserve: Land and the Commons
summary: The prairie remnant at Nassau Community College connects conservation with the history of Native and Black Long Islanders’ access to the Hempstead commons.
address_label: Hempstead Plains Preserve, Nassau Community College, Garden City
ancestral_territory_note: A surviving part of the Hempstead Plains, whose commons supported Native and Black Long Islanders.
why_this_matters: The remaining prairie makes the history of the commons tangible. Learning who depended on this land, and who lost access to it, adds a human history to the work of protecting its grasses and wildlife.
introduction_content: Hempstead Plains Preserve at Nassau Community College protects a surviving prairie landscape amid roads, parking lots, and development. Friends of Hempstead Plains maintains the habitat and provides research and education programs.
history_content:
In a 2025 Stony Brook University lecture, historian Jennifer L. Anderson described how Native and Black Long Islanders relied on the wider Hempstead commons for grazing and other resources despite exclusion from formal land ownership. Nineteenth-century enclosure and land sales restricted those livelihoods.

The prairie at Nassau Community College is a surviving remnant of this once much larger landscape.

Preserving the Prairie

The preserve’s stewards trace their organizing to 2001, when Nassau Community College faculty led by biology professor Betsy Gulotta sought protection for the remaining grassland. Friends of Hempstead Plains incorporated in 2003 to manage the preserve and support education.
whereintheworld_content: Hempstead Plains Preserve is on the Nassau Community College campus. Check Friends of Hempstead Plains for trail access and public programs.
